title: Replace with pronouns
subtitle: Swap the underlined words for y, en, le, la, les, lui, leur, stressed pronouns and more

tags.pc-agreement: le, la, les in the passé composé (agreement)
tags.stressed: moi, toi, lui, elle, eux... after a preposition
tags.double: Two pronouns together (le lui, y en...)
tags.possessive: le mien, le tien, la sienne...

why.direct: A direct object (no preposition) becomes le, la, l' or les. It goes right before the verb.
why.pc-agreement: In the passé composé the pronoun goes before avoir, and the participle agrees with it: l'ai vue, les ai faites.
why.indirect: À + a person becomes lui (one person) or leur (several). It goes right before the verb.
why.me-te: Me, te, nous and vous work as direct and indirect objects. Before a vowel me and te become m' and t'.
why.y: Y replaces a place or à + a thing. It goes right before the verb.
why.en: En replaces de + a thing, or a quantity. With a number or quantity the number stays: j'en ai trois.
why.stressed: After a preposition, and after à or de with a person, use moi, toi, lui, elle, nous, vous, eux, elles.
why.double: Order before the verb: me, te, nous, vous, then le, la, les, then lui, leur, then y, then en.
why.mixed: People after à: lui or leur (or à + stressed with penser à, s'intéresser à). Things after à: y. Things after de: en. People after de: de + stressed.
why.imperative: In a positive command the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen. In a negative command it stays before the verb.
why.possessive: A possessive pronoun replaces a possessive + noun: le mien, la tienne, les siens, la nôtre, les vôtres, le leur.
why.demonstrative: Celui, celle, ceux and celles replace a noun that is followed by de or a relative clause.
why.qui: Qui replaces the subject of the second sentence.
why.que: Que replaces the object of the second sentence; the participle then agrees with it.
why.ou: Où replaces a place or a time.
why.dont: Dont replaces de + a noun (parler de, avoir besoin de, le père de...).
